Bielsk Podlaski Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bielsk Podlaski, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Bielsk Podlaski from the 15th-16th centuries, though significant settlement began only after 1802; by 1921, 2,392 Jews were mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. Before this cemetery's likely mid-19th-century founding (coinciding with the religious community's formal establishment), local Jews were buried in nearby Orla. Germans carried out executions on-site during the war; in 1945-1946, survivors relocated exhumed Holocaust victims' remains from around the town here, and burials continued briefly postwar - Ajzyk Blumental was interred in 1947. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964. A 1967 monument commemorates Holocaust victims; in 2019, the Foundation for the Preservation of the Heritage of the Bielsko Region built a wall incorporating three recovered destroyed matzevot.
